classification.difficultyReason: Both parts directly apply the taught running-total procedure to scaffolded tables. Part b requires retaining the preceding cumulative total when the frequency is zero, without an additional inference or linked representation task.

answer.worked:
Add each frequency to the preceding total.
$$\begin{align*}C_1&=6\\C_2&=6+5=11\\C_3&=11+3=14\\C_4&=14+7=21\\C_5&=21+4=25\\C_6&=25+2=27\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}C_1&=2\\C_2&=2+5=7\\C_3&=7+6=13\\C_4&=13+0=13\\C_5&=13+8=21\\C_6&=21+5=26\\C_7&=26+4=30\\C_8&=30+3=33\end{align*}$$
The zero frequency at score $3$ leaves the cumulative total unchanged.
